title: Skep — Cross-device collaboration for AI coding agents
excerpt: Your agents, on every device, in one live session. Cross-device collaboration via join-code sessions. @skepagent/skep v0.2.0, now with Skills.
content_html:
@skepagent/skep v0.2.0

Your agents, on every device, in one live session.

Cross-device collaboration for AI coding agents via live join-code sessions. Each peer runs its own agent — Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and more.

Apache-2.0 · Node.js ≥ 22.12 · macOS & Linux · bin: skep

One master, many peers

Start a session, peers join with a code, and work flows between devices. Each peer runs an AI coding agent in its own repo.

/orchestrate

$ skep
> /start
join code 7391-4820-1940 · 192.168.1.20:7419
+ device, server, ios, android, h5 joined
> /orchestrate auto
→ split into briefs, dispatched to peers
> /orchestrate confirm
? proposed briefs, waiting for your confirm
> /orchestrate off
→ no auto-split, you route work yourself
✓ 5 peers reported back
✓ summary received · changed files listed
✓ summary received · changed files listed

Illustrative session. Repo names, devices and output are examples, not measurements.

Up in three steps

Run Skep inside any git repository on each device.

  1. 1

    Start a session

    On the master device, run skep and start a session. You get a join code and an address.

    /start

  2. 2

    Join from another device

    In the peer TUI, /join with the code and address. Any repo checkout works. Optional --role if using a skill.

    /join 7391-4820-1940 192.168.1.20:7419

  3. 3

    Hand out the work

    Let the orchestrator split work (auto / confirm / off), or send an intent yourself.

    /orchestrate auto

Also: skep session start · skep session join · /orchestrate confirm|off · /skills · optional /start --skill <id>

What's new in v0.2: Skills

Packaged workflows with roles, stages and checks. Optional — plain sessions still work. List with /skills, pick with /skill use. Default skill is generic; featured example is iot-ble-feature.

Featured example

iot-ble-feature

One BLE feature across the C++ device layer, server HTTP API, iOS, Android and H5: one shared contract, a brief per role, and a cross-stack consistency check.

  • device
  • server
  • ios
  • android
  • h5

contract → providers → clients · clients optional

/skill use iot-ble-feature

CLI default

generic

Any repos, any split. The orchestrator as it worked in v0.1.15: refine the request, brief each repo, summarize.

/skill off

Team-defined

Your own

Put a skill in .skep/skills/ to share roles, prompts and checks with your team. Project skills need a one-time /skill trust.

.skep/skills/<id>/skill.toml

Skep works on the software layer in your repos. Hardware, bench and real-device testing stay with your team.

What's in v0.2

Skills

/skills and /skill use|off|show. Ships with generic (default) and iot-ble-feature.

Role binding

Peers join with --role; fix any mapping with /skill bind.

Staged briefs

Briefs follow the skill's stages, and every role brief carries the same contract.

Cross-stack check

The summary compares what each role reported and names what needs a human.

Slim join

One line, /join <code> <ip:port>, from any repo checkout.

Orchestrator

/orchestrate auto|confirm|off|new. Default is auto.

TUI and browser UI

Split panels with /layout split, scrollback, or skep ui in a browser.

Protocol v2

Output sharing is opt-in, summaries list changed files, and briefs go up to 8000.

D19

Your logins stay with each device's agent

Each device runs its own agent (claude, codex or pi) with its own login. Skep does not actively detect, record, or upload your provider keys or tokens, and a peer shares live output only if you opt in.
